newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - back to unchanged after Fed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - back to unchanged after Fed.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond secondary market prices gave back slight gains scored prior to the Federal Open Market Committee's interest rate rise, moving back to unchanged near the end of Tuesday's session.
Traders said the muni cash market was never as high as Treasuries, which had been more than 1/2 point higher prior to the Fed's announcement it had raised the Fed funds rate 25 basis points.
At best, muni cash was about 1/8 to 1/4 higher prior to the announcement, and was back to unchanged afterward, market participants said.
The government long bond, in contrast, moved into negative territory after the announcement. It was down 14/32 at 95-26/32 to yield 6.96 percent.
In new issue action Tuesday, Smith Barney Inc. repriced Delaware State Housing Authority's $43 million bond deal, lowering yields five basis points in some maturities.
On the competitive side, Prudential Securities Inc. won $39 million Connecticut Health and Educational Facilities Authority bonds, reoffering the 2017 maturity at a 5.642 percent yield.

In the futures markets, the June municipal bond futures contract ended 9/32 lower at 113-1/32, while the June Treasury bond contract lost 8/32 to 108-23/32. The MOB spread narrowed to 138 ticks from 139 at the close on Monday.

In secondary market activity, Dade County, Fla., FGIC water and sewer system revenue bonds of October 2026, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.77 percent, down two basis points from Monday.
Jefferson County, Ala., FGIC sewer revenue bonds of February 2027, which pay a 5-3/4 percent coupon, were bid at 97-3/4, down 1/8.
Municipal bond sales for Wednesday are expected to total $1.1 billion in 30 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $921 million in 19 sales, with a $600 million Hawaii deal through Smith Barney Inc. topping the the list.
On the competitive side, 11 sales totaling $164 million are on the schedule, a $45 million Oakland, Calif., deal at 1300 EST is the largest.
